title: Unsigned letter to Anne de Montmorency, 1536, BnF fr. 3053 ff. 85-87 with its contemporary decipherment on f. 86 (DECODE R4248; second fr. 3053 cipher)

transcription.notes: About 20 cipher lines (2 on P2, ~11 on P3, ~9 on P5) in a second fr. 3053 cipher, not Mâcon's. The cipher was not transcribed sign by sign; the contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86 (P8-P9) was transcribed (about 85 % of words secure, a few [?]).

system.summary: Substitution on graphic signs with homophones and nulls (30, the triple-barred cross, 22), matching Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table (img/francisMacon2.png); not 'Mascon's cipher'.
system.sibling_key: none applied: Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table (cryptiana francis.htm) identified as this cipher's; Mascon's cipher tested and gives nonsense.
system.notes: Nulls per Tomokiyo's table: 30, ǂ, 22. Signs seen: ǂ, W, ~, α, ∞, Ɛ, ꝗ, looped ʃ, φ, #, 11, z, k, 30. Not tabulated here: the f. 86 decipherment makes it unnecessary.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary clear decipherment of the passage on f. 86 of the same volume; Tomokiyo notes the f. 85 fragment is 'deciphered on f. 86' (cryptiana francis.htm). No printed plaintext.

conditions.human_role: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images

solution.what: Fetched the R4248 page crops (P2-P9) from DECODE with the stored cookie, as part of catalogue item 180 (rome1536).
Applied Mâcon's key (Mascon's cipher, macon_key.md: W = LL, ~ = null, 30 = pape) to f. 85: nonsense.
Matched the glyph set to Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table (nulls 30, ǂ, 22; R = W; O = 3; U = α); 'ꭓ m Ɛ 3 30 11 ǂ' after 'et partant' starts JE LE CO[NSEILLOIS] as in the decipherment.
Transcribed the full contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86 (P8-P9), about 85 % of words secure; it agrees with every clear connecting phrase left on f. 85.

Split from rome1536 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R4248 is in a second fr. 3053 cipher and was read from its contemporary decipherment, not with Mascon's cipher; its own entry, with R4248.md and Tomokiyo's second table moved here.

outcome.method_basis: The passage was read from the contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86, checked against the clear connecting words on f. 85; the cipher's key was identified (Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table) but not applied or tabulated.
outcome.fraction_read_source: The f. 86 decipherment covers the whole cipher passage; R4248.md transcribes it with about 85 % of words secure (a handful marked [?]). No sign-level count.
outcome.notes: Read from the contemporary decipherment on f. 86: the writer, after a day in the country with a cardinal ('Carafe'?), urged that everything, above all the war, pass through Montmorency's hands; the cardinal of Lorraine had conceded too much in his capitulation with the pope. Writer unidentified (no signature on the crops).

credits.note: clear decipherment of the f. 85 cipher on f. 86
second fr. 3053 table and the note that the f. 85 fragment is deciphered on f. 86 (cryptiana francis.htm)
